clue.text: Virus infection in birds sounds awful nuisance

indicators.note: sounds tells us the following phrase is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: awful means foul, and a nuisance is a pest

explanation.surface: Birds are struck down by a virus that is a terrible pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl pest is a name for avian influenza and Newcastle disease, viral diseases of poultry.

clue.text: Litter dropped by swine producing long dispute

parts.note: far means a long way
a row is a dispute

explanation.surface: Pig litter causing a lengthy argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sow's brood of piglets is called by this name, and the verb means to give birth to them.

clue.text: Flat is cleaned inside

explanation.surface: An apartment is given a thorough internal clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home, but it means drained of colour or energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A faded, exhausted look is listless and pale, and a container rinsed through has had its interior cleaned.

clue.text: Quiet promenade bringing couples together

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an airing is a stroll taken for fresh air, a promenade

explanation.surface: A peaceful seaside walk where people pair off.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching people or things in twos is putting them into couples.

clue.text: Seeing that evil dominates the church

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for evil sits over the church, so it dominates it

parts.note: sin is evil
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Because wickedness holds sway over the church.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction it means because or given that.

clue.text: Game that's possibly based on pontoon …

explanation.surface: A card game that may have grown out of pontoon, the blackjack-like game.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is a British card game, so the surface suggests a card game descended from it; the second sense is a structure carried on pontoons, floating supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is a card game, and a floating crossing laid on boats or floats is a pontoon span.

clue.text: Broadcast from early edition cut off

indicators.note: off says the letters are not right, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ed is the shortened form of edition

explanation.surface: A broadcast taken from a morning edition that was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' looks like one phrase, but 'cut' shortens edition to ED and 'off' rearranges EARLY plus ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme passed on from one transmitter to others has been transmitted onward.

clue.text: Over the top I had erected something similar

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the pieces are set upright, read from the bottom up

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: An excessive figure set something like it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the same again, used to avoid repeating what has just been said.

clue.text: As I can represent a couple of them

definitions.text: As I can represent a couple of them

parts.words: As I can represent a couple of them
parts.note: As is the chemical symbol of arsenic and I that of iodine, so the two letters name two chemical substances

explanation.surface: A sentence about what the speaker is able to stand for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As I' reads as 'since I', but they are symbols from the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic and iodine are basic chemical substances listed in the periodic table.

clue.text: How Robin looked with a squint

parts.note: Cock Robin of the nursery rhyme, a cock being a male bird
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: The way the robin peered, squinting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone squinting has eyes that do not line up, which is crooked or askew.

clue.text: … and another that's likely to go to sudden death finish

definitions.text: … and another that's likely to go to sudden death finish

parts.words: … and another that's likely to go to sudden death finish
parts.note: continuing from the previous clue, another game, this one where a round can end with the player dead

explanation.surface: Another game, one that tends to be settled by a sudden-death decider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sudden death' sounds like a sporting tie-break, but here the loser really dies: a revolver with one bullet is spun and fired at the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This deadly gamble with a single-bullet revolver is a game in which a turn can end in actual death.

clue.text: Former unit returned discharge

parts.note: one is a unit, the single number

indicators.note: returned means the word for discharge is read backwards

parts.note: to discharge is to emit

explanation.surface: A former army unit sent back after being discharged.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-time champion is a former champion: the compound adjective means previous or erstwhile.

clue.text: Sort of surgery that enabled the butler to see

definitions.text: that enabled the butler to see

explanation.surface: An operation technique, and a nosy servant spying on the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Minimally invasive surgery through small cuts has this name; the stock eavesdropping butler peers through a door's lock opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery done through tiny incisions is so called, and the small opening in a lock is what a snooping servant peeps through.

clue.text: Young man after money, a belligerent American

indicators.note: after puts the young man behind the money in the answer

parts.note: dough is slang for money
a boy is a young man

explanation.surface: A youth chasing riches, described as an aggressive American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belligerent' here means taking part in a war, not quarrelsome: the word was a nickname for a US infantryman in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname was given to American foot soldiers in the First World War, combatants in that conflict.

clue.text: In France, he gets into golf club in an impudent way

indicators.note: gets into puts the French word for he inside the golf club

parts.note: a brassy is an old wooden golf club with a brass sole
il is French for he

explanation.surface: A Frenchman cheekily forces his way into a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is cheek or nerve, so acting with brass is behaving with insolent nerve.

clue.text: Took the underground back, coming out here?

indicators.note: back means the verb for travelling by underground is read backwards

parts.note: to tube is to travel on the London Underground, known as the Tube

explanation.surface: Someone took the Tube home and emerged at this station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway. 'Coming out' is the society or stage sense of a first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A first public appearance, such as a debutante's entry into society, is a coming out.

clue.text: Orchestra getting on dressing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra
getting on means growing older, ageing

explanation.surface: An orchestra is getting dressed before a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping a wound in gauze is applying a dressing to it.

clue.text: Cavalry officer on magnificent bay

explanation.surface: A cavalry officer mounted on a fine bay horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' suggests a horse's colour, but it is Cardigan Bay on the coast of Wales; the 7th Earl led the Charge of the Light Brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl commanded the Light Brigade in the Crimean War, and the great Welsh inlet carries the same name.

clue.text: Continue imitating Miss Bell

explanation.surface: Keep on mimicking a woman called Miss Bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Brontë published under the pen name Acton Bell, as her sisters were Currer and Ellis Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep acting is to carry on performing, and Anne Brontë's pseudonym was Acton Bell.

clue.text: Sitting on the fence in colourless gear

explanation.surface: Someone undecided wearing drab clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' reads as clothing but is the position of a gearbox with no gear engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking no side, having no strong colour, and the disengaged gearbox position all share this word.

clue.text: Supports for wood and metal clubs

parts.note: irons are metal-headed golf clubs

explanation.surface: Golf equipment that holds up timber and steel clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' tempts the golf reading of a wooden club, but it is firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedogs are metal stands that hold logs up in a fireplace.

clue.text: Thoroughgoing revolutionary

explanation.surface: A complete rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means affecting the fundamental nature of something, and the noun is someone seeking extreme political change.

clue.text: A second English degree for very changeable type

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A student taking a second English degree is a fickle character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very changeable' is literal: the organism constantly alters its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled organism keeps changing shape as it moves, so it is the classic shape-shifter.

clue.text: Debate sounds as if it's a sporting event

indicators.note: sounds says the word for the sporting event is heard spoken, not read

parts.note: the discus is an athletics throwing event

explanation.surface: Arguing over something that seems like a competitive sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a matter through with others is to talk it over.

clue.text: Source of strength one revealed in news broadcast

indicators.note: revealed in puts the letter for one inside the rearranged news
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of news are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A source of power exposed in a news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns NEWS into SNEW, and 'revealed in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is tough tissue, and figuratively it means muscle or power.

clue.text: Is it useless for those fighting at the front?

definitions.text: Is it useless for those fighting at the front?

parts.words: Is it useless for those fighting at the front?
parts.note: the question suggests a weapon carried at the side, not borne out in front, asking whether frontline troops can use it

explanation.surface: A question about whether some weapon is of any use to frontline soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A pistol worn on the belt at one's side is the weapon; 'front' plays against its being carried at the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol or sword worn at the belt is a personal weapon carried on the hip.

clue.text: Rising shares hanger-on depends on

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for shares is read from the bottom up

parts.note: parts are shares

explanation.surface: A clinger relies on rising share prices.
explanation.walkthrough: A strap-hanger is a standing passenger gripping a strap on a bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing commuters hold the looped band hanging from the ceiling, hence strap-hangers.

clue.text: Training with anaesthetic in medical group

parts.note: a general is a general anaesthetic, which puts the patient fully under
practice is training by repetition

explanation.surface: Training in anaesthesia within a medical team.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a GP (family doctor) works in such a practice, a group of doctors sharing a surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A family doctors' surgery, often several physicians working together, is known by this name in Britain.

clue.text: With rail connections, they stand by for flights

definitions.text: With rail connections, they stand by for flights

parts.words: With rail connections, they stand by for flights
parts.note: reads like airport transport links, but means posts joined to a banister that stand at the foot or turn of a staircase

explanation.surface: Transport hubs linked to the railway, waiting beside departing aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flights' are flights of stairs and 'rail' is the handrail, not trains or planes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the posts at the ends of a staircase that support its handrail.

clue.text: Self-defence as justified by Newman

explanation.surface: A self-defence argument as made by Cardinal Newman.
explanation.walkthrough: John Henry Newman's spiritual autobiography is titled 'Apologia Pro Vita Sua', a defence of his own life.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct, as in Newman's famous book.
